Thanks again for your time today — appreciate the candid discussion and the team's openness about priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have one shared thread to work from.

Attendees (from today):
- Rajiv Menon (AcroHealth) — product/economic buyer
- Aditi Kapoor (AcroHealth) — procurement lead
- Maya Iqbal (AcroHealth) — security reviewer
- Diego Fernandez (Redwood) — lead AE
- Ben Carter (Redwood) — solutions engineer
- Marissa Cole (Redwood) — customer success (intro)

Key decision criteria you mentioned:
- Latency P50/P95 for 512-token prompts (must be <150ms P50 in US-EAST)
- Deterministic auditing & immutable request logs (for clinical traceability)
- On-prem / VPC deployment option for PHI workflows
- Clear unit economics and committed pricing for reserved capacity

Security/procurement gates we discussed: SOC 2 Type II report, vendor risk questionnaire, Data Processing Agreement (DPA), and a standard PO/contract cycle.

Action items I propose:
1) AcroHealth to confirm full buying committee + primary reviewer for each gate (economic/technical/security/legal/procurement).
2) Redwood to deliver an itemized procurement packet (SOC2 summary, DPA template, short SSO/KMS architecture note) by EOD tomorrow — I attached the SOC2 summary and demo recording for reference.
3) Set a 30-minute procurement sync with Aditi + Tom (legal/procurement) early next week to walk the questionnaire.

Please reply with names, emails, and desired review windows for each stakeholder so we can map a realistic procurement timeline. If it helps, I sketched a minimal mutual action plan we can iterate on once you confirm stakeholders.

Attachments: redwood-demo-recording-20270628.mp4 (recording link stub), redwood-security-SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks —
